name: zero-cost-calibration-and-harness-ablation
selection: Every resolved single market event with a finite frozen crowd probability in the registered rounds; exclude every source/question ID exposed in the local archive through July 5. Keep repeated eligible event/round forecasts, cluster intervals by source/question; report round signs too.
training: Earliest forecast per source/question, issued and resolved before 2026-01-01 in the available archive. Development: new source/question IDs issued January-June 2026 and resolved before July. Nominal settlement dates are not independently attested label-publication times; this remains a retrospective mechanical replay.
forecast_track: crowd-aware deterministic calibration, not an LLM or crowd-free skill test

methods.candidate: existing source-offset fitter on incumbent, min_n=25, shrink_n=75; frozen residual logit offsets, no refit

primary: candidate minus incumbent mean Brier on matched eligible forecasts, lower is better

development.candidate_fitting_exposure: 9 candidate policies inspected on development; not an unseen result.

harness_checks: scoring-only baselines must not enter any inference-stage prompt
valid positive Bayesian likelihoods must not become impossible by floating-point underflow
all registered benchmark rows and event clusters must be retained
score throughput at 1000/5000 cases with exact score and bootstrap agreement
limits: No paid or local LLM inference; no old-checkpoint judgment claim.
Existing archived old-checkpoint studies remain unmodified.
A public dataset commit is a reproducibility pin, not an independent preregistration witness.
Public round question sets may repeat semantically related events; ID exclusion does not remove all dependence.
Dataset-derived numerical inputs retain ForecastBench CC BY-SA 4.0; code MIT.
No leaderboard submission or top-rank claim.
